# Implementation Plan: Ubiquitous Messaging Platform

**Branch**: `001-ubiquitous-messaging-platform` | **Date**: 2025-11-26 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-ubiquitous-messaging-platform/spec.md`

**Note**: This plan was generated by the `/speckit.plan` command on 2025-11-26. See `.specify/templates/commands/plan.md` for the execution workflow.

## Summary

**Primary Requirement**: Build a distributed messaging platform API capable of routing text messages and files (up to 2 GB) between users in 1:1 private and group conversations, with persistent server storage, delivery state tracking (SENT → DELIVERED → READ), real-time streaming, and horizontal scalability to support millions of concurrent users.

**Technical Approach** (from research.md):
- **API Layer**: gRPC with Protobuf 3.25.3 for 30-40% lower latency vs REST JSON, strong typing, and native bidirectional streaming
- **Message Broker**: Apache Kafka with partition-based ordering (conversation_id as partition key) for at-least-once delivery, high throughput (millions msg/sec), and log persistence
- **Persistence**: MongoDB with embedded documents (state_history arrays), write concern: majority for durability, indexed queries (<200ms p95 for 50-message pagination)
- **File Storage**: MinIO (P2 deferred) with tus resumable upload protocol, chunk-based transfer (5 MB chunks), stateless server design
- **Multi-Platform**: Telegram Bot API (one real integration, P4 deferred) + mock adapters for WhatsApp/Instagram to demonstrate plugin architecture without commercial API costs

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Java 17 (LTS)  
**Primary Dependencies**: Spring Boot 3.2.5, gRPC 1.64.0, Protobuf 3.25.3, Spring Kafka 3.1.x, Spring Data MongoDB 4.2.x  
**Storage**: MongoDB 7.0 (replica set with 3 nodes for HA per NFR-011), MinIO (P2 - deferred to post-POC for file storage)  
**Testing**: JUnit 5 + Mockito + Testcontainers (MongoDB, Kafka, RabbitMQ containers for integration tests)  
**Target Platform**: Linux server (Docker Compose for development, Kubernetes for production scaling)
**Project Type**: Single backend API (gRPC server + Kafka consumers, no separate frontend)  
**Performance Goals**: <100ms p95 latency for message submission (FR-012, NFR-012), 1000 concurrent gRPC connections per instance (NFR-002), 2 second real-time delivery for online users (NFR-015)  
**Constraints**: 10,000 concurrent active users in MVP baseline (NFR-001), 99.9% uptime target (NFR-007), at-least-once delivery guarantee (FR-026), max 2 GB file size (FR-024)  
**Scale/Scope**: P1 MVP (text messaging + 1:1 conversations), P2 (file uploads + webhooks), P3 (group conversations), P4 (multi-platform routing with Telegram + mocks)

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

| Principle | Gate Check | Status | Notes |
|-----------|------------|--------|-------|
| **I. Educational Code Quality** | All classes have JavaDoc explaining distributed systems concepts | ✅ PASS | Spec emphasizes educational mission (UFG students), code must demonstrate patterns (async messaging, eventual consistency, idempotency). Classes will include concept documentation. |
| **II. Explicit Responsibility** | Every class declares single responsibility, bounded context documented | ✅ PASS | Hexagonal architecture planned (ports & adapters), domain services isolated from infrastructure. Each service will document what it does NOT handle. |
| **III. Descriptive Naming** | No abbreviations, self-documenting code, boolean prefixes | ✅ PASS | Constitution explicitly prohibits `msg`, `conn`, `req` abbreviations. Variable names like `incomingMessage`, `isMessageValid`, `maximumRetryAttempts` required. |
| **IV. Test-Driven Development** | Tests written before implementation, contract tests for Protobuf, Testcontainers for integration | ✅ PASS | Spec requires 80% coverage minimum (NFR implicit). Contract tests mandatory for all gRPC endpoints. Integration tests will use Testcontainers (MongoDB, Kafka) per constitution. |
| **V. Performance with Scalability** | Stateless services, indexed queries, async I/O, connection pools sized | ✅ PASS | Spec defines <100ms p95 latency (NFR-012), 10k concurrent users (NFR-001), horizontal scaling (NFR-006). MongoDB indexes documented in data-model.md. Kafka connection pool limited to 50/instance. |
| **VI. Clear Architecture** | Technology choices in `decisions.md`, no magic frameworks, versioning strategy | ✅ PASS | research.md documents all architectural decisions (gRPC vs REST, Kafka vs RabbitMQ, MongoDB vs PostgreSQL) with rationale and alternatives. Protobuf package versioning: `chat_api.v1` → `chat_api.v2`. |
| **VII. Documentation-First** | Feature docs in `docs/features/`, runbooks, auto-generated API docs, commit message format | ✅ PASS | quickstart.md provides Docker Compose setup. contracts/README.md explains Protobuf generation. gRPC Server Reflection enabled for runtime API discovery (per NFR-023). |
| **VIII. Incremental Delivery** | POC-first development, layer-by-layer construction, standard library reuse, realistic external dependencies | ✅ PASS | Spec defines P1 (MVP core), P2 (file uploads), P3 (groups), P4 (multi-platform). POC validates API→Kafka→MongoDB flow first. Uses tus protocol (standard) for resumable uploads. Telegram (real) + WhatsApp/Instagram (mocked) per constitution principle. |

**Overall Assessment**: ✅ **ALL GATES PASS** - No constitution violations detected. Project aligns with educational mission, follows incremental delivery (P1→P4 phasing), and uses standard patterns (hexagonal architecture, event-driven messaging, TDD).

**Structure Decision**: Selected **Option 1: Single Project** (backend API only) because:
1. No separate frontend/mobile client in scope - this is a backend API platform
2. Aligns with hexagonal architecture (domain isolated from adapters)
3. Simplifies dependency management (single pom.xml)
4. gRPC + REST coexist in same Spring Boot application (gRPC for messaging, REST for file uploads P2)
